A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe X-Dub. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed components and relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, a 30-participant user study, ablations, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a reference-frame-count experiment in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The two-stage DiT framework and multi-phase objectives remain. However, v2 changes the generator from single-reference conditioning to multiple references, selecting four by default, and replaces the full-face 3DMM mask with its lower-half portion (Section 3.1; Appendices A.3 and B.2). These are limited procedural changes.

E1.justification: Training data, HDTF, and the 440-pair benchmark retain their coverage; ContextDubBench is renamed X-DubBench. Section 4.2 newly reports identity and color stability on videos longer than one minute, a limited extension of documented evaluation scenarios, although no separate sample counts or quantitative results accompany it.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain Wav2Lip, VideoReTalking, TalkLip, IP-LAP, Diff2Lip, MuseTalk, LatentSync, and the renamed generator baseline. The timing comparison also retains its comparator set, including MultiTalk. The new reference-count experiment is an internal ablation.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an HDTF experiment varying reference counts across 1, 2, 4, and 6 with 25-frame segments. Appendix E revises accelerated inference from removing approximately 10 early steps to using 25 total steps by pruning early and late stages. The standard 50-step timing comparison remains unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 and Table 6 test reference-count sensitivity and justify selecting four references. Existing conditioning, training-phase, segment-length, and timestep ablations remain. The 20-pair bootstrapping analysis moves from Section 4.1/Table 4 to Appendix F.2/Table 11; it is not newly added.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains identical MOS values and 95% confidence intervals. Neither version reports model-run variability, seeds, or significance tests. New success-rate voting details document annotation procedures without adding uncertainty or inter-rater reliability estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports reference-count results: one versus four references gives FID 8.01 versus 7.72, LPIPS 0.025 versus 0.020, and CSIM 0.892 versus 0.904. Section 4.2 adds the longer-than-one-minute stability finding. All ten original tables retain their numerical results after matching renumbering and relocation; no headline performance gain between versions is established.

T1.justification: The flow-matching equations, conditioning mathematics, and single-step denoising derivation remain substantively unchanged. Introducing tau as min(t, t_thres) restates the existing clipping formula. The added attention-cost explanation does not introduce a substantive formal result or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same central contributions: constructing synthetic-real pairs with a mask-based generator, training a mask-free editor, using timestep-adaptive multi-phase learning, and introducing a challenging benchmark with strong empirical performance. The shift from context-rich self-bootstrapping terminology to generative bootstrapping largely reframes these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking short-segment processing to reduced attention cost and interprets reference-count gains as saturating beyond four, motivating a quality–cost tradeoff. Appendix A.3 also adds a rationale for retaining background context through lower-half masks. Existing interpretations of bootstrapping and phase specialization largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies A100 hardware and documents success-rate scoring by 10 evaluators, with at least five judgments per video and majority voting. It replaces the project-page link with explicit code/demo repository information, whose availability is not independently verified. Conversely, v1's specification of 50% motion-conditioning dropout is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds KeySync, RASA, and HuMo references and removes AlignHuman and the AV-HuBERT reference. The introduction additionally contrasts generated pseudo-pairs with scalability and domain-gap limitations of 3D-rendered alternatives. The broader positioning against mask-based dubbing remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around an explicit two-stage narrative. Generator/editor terminology becomes G_mask/G_free, the title and benchmark name change, method subsections are reorganized, and bootstrapping validation moves into an expanded experimental appendix.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned, Figures 4 and 5 are regrouped, and Figure 10's study interface is replaced. Tables are relocated and renumbered, a reference-count table is added, and several retained appendix illustrations are enlarged or separated.

improvement.justification: The new reference-count ablation provides concrete support for selecting four references, while hardware and success-rate documentation improve reproducibility. The revised narrative and pipeline figure clarify the two stages. These gains are limited and partly offset by the omitted motion-dropout specification and Appendix B.2's overstated monotonic-improvement description: Table 6 shows CSIM decreasing slightly from four to six references. The principal empirical evidence remains unchanged.
